history.period: Rashtrakuta era (claim unverified; Ganj Golai market laid out 1917)
history.summary: The Jagdamba Mata temple stands at the centre of Latur's circular Ganj Golai market. According to the Latur district administration (latur.gov.in), the temple was built in the Rashtrakuta era and is regarded as a section/shrine of Tuljapur's Tuljabhavani Temple. The Ganj Golai market around it was laid out in 1917 by town planner Faiyajuddin (engineer Fayyazuddin), with 16 roads radiating from the central structure. A Navratri mahostav is celebrated at the temple every year with great fervour, when the surrounding markets fill with traditional wares and food. NOTE: the Rashtrakuta-era claim for the temple and the 1917 date for the market structure come from different sources and should not be conflated. Coordinates are from a full-address geocode match (Ganj Golai, Latur 413512); the founding date is approximate and unverified.

name: Jagdamba Mata Temple, Ganj Golai
town_description: Latur (ancient Lattalur) is a historic city in the Marathwada region of Maharashtra, set in the Manjra–Tawarja valley between the Manjra and Tawarja rivers. It was developed by the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I and is known for its distinctive circular Ganj Golai market (1917), the Siddheshwar–Ratneshwar temples, and the 6th-century Kharosa caves nearby. Today it is a major educational and wholesale trade (oilseeds) hub of Marathwada.
